newsitem.title: GERMANY: German AgMin details Oder flood damage to farms.
newsitem.headline: German AgMin details Oder flood damage to farms.

text.p: Three weeks of floods in eastern Germany's Brandenburg state have threatened the financial survival of 30 farms on a total of 12,000 hectares, the agriculture ministry said in a press release.

Some 7,200 ha were submerged in the Ziltendorfer basin area near Neuzelle and another 4,500 ha in the Oderbruch, a low-lying region below the swollen Oder river, were too soaked to allow the harvesting of crops this year.
Ground water levels would remain high for the near future and autumn plantings for the 1998 harvest would almost certainly be impossible.
Raised Oder river levels had threatened to break weakened dikes which at one stage could have flooded more than 75,000 hectares. But water levels have at last started to retreat.

Farm minister Jochen Borchert welcomed immediate European Union Commission aid of three million marks and a decision to release 86 million marks from EU regional aid funds to help clear up the devastated area.
Borchert said the Bonn government and German states were all aiming to secure optimal help for Brandenburg. They had deferred tax claims and provided cheap credits.
Talks were continuing to secure more EU aid, for example to strengthen and renew weakened flood walls.
The EU had also been asked to make some 30 million marks in rescheduled autumn farm support payments available for immediate release.

Livestock evacuations had resulted in transport, housing, feeds, labour and vaccinations costs, the farm ministry said. Dairy yields and feeding ratios from evacuated animals had worsened because of the disruptions.
